sense: keep, not lose or give up

terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, with the accusative
evidence: Cic. Quinct. 59: ut amīcōs observantiā, rem parsimōniā retinēret (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Amic. 70: retinent tamen cāritātem in pāstōrēs
terms.comment: Keep what one has: friends, property, a custom, one’s dignity, a sense of proportion. Its first sense is “hold back, detain” (quid mē retinēs?, Plaut. Ep. 1.1.61) and so “restrain” (Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, with the accusative
terms.comment: The plain verb for holding; memoriā tenēre is “remember”. See hold on.

phrases.latin: ut amīcōs observantiā, rem parsimōniā retinēret
phrases.english: to keep his friends by attentiveness and his property by thrift

phrases.latin: lūdendī etiam est quīdam modus retinendus
phrases.english: even in play a certain limit must be kept

phrases.latin: cum cognitī sunt et aut deōrum aut rēgum fīliī inventī, retinent tamen cāritātem in pāstōrēs, quōs patrēs multōs annōs esse dūxērunt
phrases.english: when they have been recognised and found to be sons of gods or kings, they still keep their love for the shepherds they took for their fathers for many years

sources: Lewis & Short: retineo · Lewis & Short: teneo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 336.
